subject: Draft: IaC dependency graph + credential validation playbook for private deployments
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@acmeinfra.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: IaC dependency graph + credential validation playbook for private deployments

Hi team,

Attached is a first-pass playbook and dependency graph for private deployments (VPC/on-prem). The goal is to have an automated CI gate that validates:
- module dependency ordering (TF/Helm/Ansible windowing)
- secrets/credentials are referenced via Vault/KMS (no inline secrets)
- preflight plan checks and idempotency smoke tests

What I need from each of you:
- Marcus: review the dependency graph and Helm umbrella notes — ensure chart hooks/ordering won't break rolling updates.
- Karthik: CI snippets for terraform/helm/ansible checks, and any pipeline performance concerns.
- Irene: Ansible idempotency checklist + runbook for blue/green failover (airgapped sites).

Attachments: iac-dep-graph-v1.svg, credential-validation-playbook-v0.3.md, pipeline-checks-examples.patch

High-level constraints from ACME (cc'd Priya): they require proof that no deploy artifact contains plaintext credentials and that the pipeline can detect stale module dependencies.

Please annotate the doc inline in Git and reply with any blockers by EOD Tuesday so we can present to ACME next week.

Thanks,
Neha

Subject: Re: Draft: IaC dependency graph + credential validation playbook for private deployments

Thanks Neha — good start. Quick notes from a Helm/TF perspective:

1) Dependency graph: the SVG looks correct for our topology but we should explicitly mark 'schema-change' modules (networking, storage) as blockers for parallel rollouts. Those need cluster-level drains and PVC handoff sequencing.

2) Helm umbrella: avoid long-running chart hooks that depend on external services. For private deploys we should prefer native post-install hooks only for non-critical sidecars. Main apps should use readiness probes + rollout.pause semantics. Add a small table in the playbook for hook policies by chart type.

3) Terraform state & module staleness: add an automated detect step that checks module source revisions (git tags/commit) and flags drift if a submodule hasn't been bumped in X weeks. We ran into a nasty drift last quarter where a module used a deprecated provider flag.

4) Secret reference patterns: +1 on Vault. For airgapped customers consider a local vault mirror pattern (read-only sync) and annotate which KMS/HSM integrations are permitted.

I added inline comments in the Drive link and attached a small patch that adds the hook policy table. Also: consider adding a 'fast-fail' flag in CI that prevents Helm umbrella from attempting to upgrade unhealthy subcharts.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-19T13:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: IaC dependency graph + credential validation playbook for private deployments

Great draft — a few CI-focused suggestions from my side:

- Terraform: run 'terraform init -backend-config=... && terraform validate && terraform plan -out=tfplan' inside a disposable runner, then use 'terraform show -json tfplan' to assert no plaintext secrets and that no resource change touches provider-level settings (networking/storage). Add a small jq script in the repo to assert sensitive values are not present.

- Helm: Add a pre-merge linter job that runs 'helm template' + kubeval against the same API version the target cluster advertises. For umbrella charts, validate that subchart upgrade order in Chart.yaml matches dependency graph ordering.

- Ansible: run dry-run with --check and a lightweight dockerized target that reproduces the OS surface (glibc, kernel modules) to detect idempotency failures. Also capture changed= output to detect unexpected stateful changes.

- Pipeline gating: I added two gate levels:
  * gating/fast: quick sanity checks (lint, terraform validate, helm lint) that must pass for fast merges.
  * gating/strict: full plan + show/json checks + ansible --check + artifact-scanning; required before any prod promotion.

I've pushed examples into the pipeline-checks-examples.patch (attached) — includes a GitLab CI snippet and a small GitHub Actions workflow that demonstrates the plan->assert->approve flow. Note: performance risk with full strict gate — we'll need cache warmers (remote state cache, helm repo cache) to keep run times acceptable for developer experience.

Happy to pair on a short testing spike.

- Karthik
From: Priya Shah <pshah@acmeinfra.com>

Subject: Re: Draft: IaC dependency graph + credential validation playbook for private deployments

Thanks Neha, Marcus, Karthik — this looks like exactly the level of rigor ACME needs. A couple of items from our security team:

- We need a binding audit report for any pipeline run that promoted to customer PROD showing the Vault policies used and the KMS key identifiers; can this be emitted as an artifact alongside the pipeline logs?
- For airgapped installations we prefer a signed artifact model for modules (sigstore/cosign) rather than relying on checksum-only verification.

Can Redwood provide a short, bulletized runbook for incident response if an IaC plan surfaces a secret or drift during the strict gate? We would like to see a play-by-play that maps to ACME's internal SIRT steps.

If possible, can Redwood deliver the updated playbook and pipeline snippets by COB Monday? We're planning a joint tabletop on Wednesday.

— Priya
Security Architect, ACME Infrastructure
pshah@acmeinfra.com

Date: 2026-07-20T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: IaC dependency graph + credential validation playbook for private deployments

Thanks all — I've incorporated the following into the playbook and pushed a new draft:

- An 'incident step' section that maps 'detection during strict gate' -> 'isolate runner & revoke temp creds' -> 'open SIRT ticket and set priority' -> 'rollback candidate generation'. I added concrete commands for revoking Vault tokens and for rotating KMS keys at a customer-specified window.

- An Ansible idempotency checklist with two tiers: quick-local checks (ansible --check + docker target) and full-run integration in a staging environment.

- A signed-artifact recommendation section: we now recommend cosign signatures for modules and added an example verify step in the CI snippet.

Action items:
- Neha: please coordinate a 30-minute spike with ACME next Monday to run the strict gate on a canary stack.
- Marcus: please add the hook-policy table to the Drive doc and call out any cluster drain preconditions.
- Karthik: finalize the CI snippet timings; we need approximate run times for both fast and strict gates so ACME can plan cadence.

I'll update the attachment names to v0.4 after we merge comments.

Irene
Irene Choi
Lead Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
